name: Solitude Mountain Resort
about: Real lifts and buildings of Solitude Mountain Resort (Big Cottonwood Canyon, Utah), researched for the 3D scenes. Lifts are keyed by OSM way id. Buildings give lat/lon (origin not fixed yet). 'verified': false marks anything not confirmed by a lift database, the resort or a photo; colours are read from dated photos and are approximate hex. Buildings are placed by lat/lon (the resort's origin is not fixed yet); 'model' is the kit model drawn there, a landmark of its own where one was built from photos; lifts carry terminal_model, the maker's hood.
notes: Lift colours are from liftblog photos dated Sep 2015 and Feb 2016, and Jan 2024 for Eagle Express.
Eagle Express (137770106) is the 2023 Doppelmayr six-pack; it replaced Utah's first detachable (1989 VonRoll/CTEC quad).
All 8 chairlifts and the one carpet are in OSM; no real lift is missing. No new lifts at Solitude on liftblog's 2024-2026 lists.
All Solitude restaurants list 'closed until winter 26/27' on 2026-11-07 (opening day Nov 20).
Two bases: Moonbeam (day lodge, Eagle/Moonbeam Express, Link, carpet) and the Village (Apex, Sunrise, Link), joined by Link.

137770106.name: Eagle Express
137770106.note: Six-pack that replaced the 1989 VonRoll/CTEC detachable quad (Utah's first detachable) in 2023; liftblog calls the stations Uni-G M. Royal-blue curved roof hood with silver-grey end and side panels, grey modern operator house at the top, galvanized towers (taller than the old lift). 85 chairs, 15 towers, top drive, 4,733 ft. Chairs silver-grey frames with black seats and puck footrests, no bubbles. Bottom station is compact, at the east end of the Moonbeam parking ('To Eagle Express' on the base map).

400353161.name: Summit Express
400353161.note: Uni-G stations: royal-blue roof with glazed panels and silver-grey ends, blue operator huts. 80 chairs, 19 towers, top drive, 5,080 ft; the line dips before climbing to the summit. A small log-cabin hut stands by the top terminal.

137770105.name: Apex Express
137770105.note: Uni-GS (Doppelmayr CTEC variant of the Uni-G): royal-blue hood with silver ribs over a glazed roof, rounded glass end, gold 'Apex EXPRESS' script on the side, blue operator huts. 52 chairs, 12 towers, top drive. Leaves from Solitude Village by Last Chance Lodge.

137770107.name: Moonbeam Express
137770107.note: Same Uni-GS look as Apex: royal-blue hood, silver-ribbed glazed roof, 'Moonbeam EXPRESS' script, blue operator huts. 64 chairs, 11 towers, top drive. Main lift out of the Moonbeam base.

137770109.name: Powderhorn II
137770109.note: Fixed quad relocated from the 2005 Moonbeam quad; black Galaxy II terminals with a glazed control cab, galvanized towers. 94 chairs, 14 towers. The Roundhouse stands just above its bottom terminal.

137770104.name: Honeycomb Return
137770104.note: Short, steep quad out of the bottom of Honeycomb Canyon; integrated drive/tension terminal at the top (black hood with skylights), fixed bullwheel return at the bottom. 9 towers, 1,300 ft. Seasonal.

137770108.name: Link
137770108.note: Short double connecting the Moonbeam base and Solitude Village; black CTEC Enterprise A-frame-leg terminal with a glazed cab, labelled 'LINK'. 56 chairs, 6 towers.

137735976.name: Sunrise
137735976.note: Beginner/intermediate triple from the village; black CTEC bottom drive/tension terminal on splayed legs with 'SUNRISE' sign, bullwheel unload at the top. 132 chairs, 17 towers. Year/maker: liftblog CTEC 1980, skiresort.info Thiokol 1977.

975730213.name: Solitude Magic Carpet
975730213.note: 44 m carpet in the Moonbeam beginner area; skiresort.info lists one 'Solitude Magic Carpet' without maker or year. A Forest Service project realigned the Moonbeam conveyor.

buildings.name: Moonbeam Lodge
buildings.style: Main day lodge at the Moonbeam base (44 x 27 m): cafeteria, Argenta Pub, rentals on the ground floor. Photos of the Moonbeam base show cream stucco walls on a split-stone base, heavy exposed timber king-post trusses over the entrances, grey shingle roofs; Little Dollie's waffle stand and the Snowsports building sit slopeside beside it. The resort calls it 'quaint but small' and planned a renovation in 2023.
buildings.note: Which of the photographed Moonbeam-base facades is the lodge itself is not certain; renovation status unconfirmed.

buildings.name: The Inn at Solitude
buildings.style: Village hotel (houses St. Bernard's and the Library Bar): terracotta/burnt-orange stucco, about five storeys, steep brown metal gable roofs with deep timber eaves and brackets, tall chimneys, white-trimmed windows with arched tops on the upper floor, stacked balconies with dark rails, a glazed single-storey pool/restaurant wing.
buildings.note: OSM says 3 levels; photos show about five.

buildings.name: Powderhorn Lodge
buildings.style: Village condo-hotel block (79 x 67 m, OSM spells it 'Powederhorn'): split-stone base, cream/tan stucco, dark red-brown timber gables and balconies, green-framed windows, timber-framed porte-cochere with the 'Powderhorn Lodge' sign. The resort's Powderhorn photos also show the village plaza clock tower: a tall square tower with a white clock face and pyramid roof over a 4-storey cream-and-timber block with green shutters.

buildings.name: Eagle Springs East
buildings.style: Large village block (97 x 56 m), home of Club Solitude: tan stucco with dark timber half-timbering, stone base, many gables and dormers, brown metal roofs, timber balconies.

buildings.name: Eagle Springs West
buildings.style: Village block (77 x 44 m): stone lower floors, tan stucco and dark timber half-timbering in the upper gables, steep brown roofs with tall gable fronts, timber balconies.

buildings.name: Creekside Condominiums
buildings.style: Village block by the creek (59 x 27 m): cream stucco, red-brown timber trim and balconies, verdigris (green copper) roofs with round turret caps, stone retaining walls and stone base.

buildings.name: Honeycomb Grill
buildings.style: Slopeside restaurant on the ground floor of village Building 4 (Suite A); wood-fired oven. Not a separate building: model as the ground floor of the village block.
buildings.note: lat/lon from the resort's dining map; OSM node 2372162405 is ~20 m away. Exterior not confirmed from a photo.

buildings.name: Solitude Village plaza
buildings.style: Car-free plaza ringed by the Inn, Powderhorn, Eagle Springs and Creekside: European-alpine mix of terracotta and cream stucco, stone bases, dark timber, steep brown or green-copper roofs, a clock tower; Stone Haus pizzeria, Thirsty Squirrel bar and the village store open onto it; ice rink in winter.
buildings.note: Centre point approximate (between Stone Haus and the Inn).

buildings.name: Last Chance Lodge
buildings.style: Slopeside lodge at the base of Apex Express (31 x 24 m, 2 levels): lunch on the main floor, Sluice Box bar upstairs, outdoor deck. Exterior look not confirmed from a photo.
buildings.note: OSM name is the old 'Last Chance Southwest Grill'.

buildings.name: The Roundhouse
buildings.style: Mid-mountain restaurant just above the Powderhorn II bottom, between Moonbeam and Eagle Express (32 x 26 m). Two-storey building on an original concrete core around a circular 360-degree fireplace; seen from the lifts it has cream/light walls, dark trim and a steep dark maroon-red faceted (multi-hip) roof, with a deck/patio. Part of it burned in April 2016 (the original core survived) and it was rebuilt/renovated; now a Himalayan-inspired cafe.
buildings.note: Only distant liftblog photos from Powderhorn II, uploaded Sep 2015 (before the 2016 fire); the current exterior after the renovation is not confirmed. Roof colour approx #7a2e34.

buildings.name: The Yurt
buildings.style: 8 m dinner yurt in the trees near the Sunrise line: round yurt with a teal-green band and white roof, plus a small timber entry cabin with a gable roof. Rebuilt in 2023.

buildings.name: The Crossings Townhomes
buildings.style: Townhome row at the village edge: cream stucco, stone, dark timber, arched windows and gables.

signature.name: Royal-blue Doppelmayr terminals
signature.description: Every detachable at Solitude wears royal blue: Apex and Moonbeam Uni-GS hoods with silver-ribbed glass roofs and gold script names, Summit and the 2023 Eagle Express six with blue roofs and silver-grey ends, plus blue operator huts.
signature.kit_note: terminal_detach exists; paint blue with silver-grey ends/ribs; gold lettering decal for Apex/Moonbeam.

signature.name: Solitude Village
signature.description: Small car-free European-style village: terracotta Inn at Solitude, Creekside's green copper turrets, half-timbered Eagle Springs, the plaza clock tower.
signature.kit_note: Needs village_block models (4-5 storey stucco/timber blocks, clock tower); base_lodge is too small.

signature.name: Black CTEC fixed-grip terminals
signature.description: Link, Sunrise, Powderhorn II and Honeycomb Return use black terminals on splayed A-frame legs with glazed cabs.

signature.name: The Roundhouse
signature.description: Maroon-roofed mid-mountain restaurant built around a round fireplace at the base of Powderhorn II.
signature.kit_note: Kit restaurant with a steep maroon faceted roof.

signature.name: The Yurt
signature.description: Dinner yurt in the trees off Sunrise.
